- Trust decision: `originFileName` (internal/bodyprocessors/multipart.go:140-148) takes only `mime.ParseMediaType`'s plain `filename`, so a non-utf-8/ascii RFC 5987 `filename*` is dropped silently and the decoy plain filename is what FILES-based rules see.
- `pattern_fit`: A (no in-repo second route: every multipart filename reaches FILES through that one call).
- Strongest lever: dual-reading — the tempting fix (make `filename*` authoritative) relocates the decoy, and the stdlib's own `dispositionParams["filename"]` is already poisoned, so the plain name must be reparsed from the raw header.
- Biggest red flag: none from O12; the real risk is that much of the published fix (charset/language variables, duplicate-header signals) is feature work not inferable from the advisory, so the gradeable surface may be narrower than the diff.
